items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: You know who was the arranger? He became big later. Gordon Jenkins. Gordon Jenkins was the arranger.

ctx.x: Was that what they called a cafeteria style?

Yeah. It was a cafeteria. So anyway I came the next day and I played for Jones and he hired me. But the guys didn’t like me. You know why they didn’t like me? They wanted away from Jones, Jones hires me, he didn’t need me, but he only used me to solo here and there. You know who was the arranger? He became big later. Gordon Jenkins. Gordon Jenkins was the arranger. So I stayed with him until let’s say around July 7th or 8th, until after Labor Day. We toured all of New England with Jones. It was cold. There were…

items.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995
items.q: Now I’ll tell you who was in the band as an arranger and became very famous. Gordon Jenkins.

ctx.x: Oh, they didn’t want another player.

No. But Ish didn’t need me, but he gave me $75 a week. And a lot of guys didn’t like it. Now I’ll tell you who was in the band as an arranger and became very famous. Gordon Jenkins. Gordon Jenkins was not known in 1933. And that’s how I happened to be with the Isham Jones band until October when he went into the Commodore Hotel in New York. He says, “Al, I have to let you go.” I says, “What’s the matter, Ish? No go?” He says, “No kid, you don’t belong to the union and you can’t do a steady job until you’re here…
Was there a trumpet player Paniccio?
